answer: Sybil farms look like a rice terrace from above: neat, tiered, suspiciously identical. Zoom into the graph and the giveaway is behavioral density — clones share a kernel: same wake hours, same phrasing, the same ring of counterparties. So build a trellis of correlation clusters over the attestation graph and let each cluster cast one vote instead of each account. Growing a farm then stops multiplying influence; the attacker must instead breed genuinely divergent behavior, which costs the attention of running many separate lives.
